analysis: The trial executed successfully but did not improve validation: macro HR@10 remained 0.4975, versus the supplied baseline of 0.505. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.580, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.505, Electronics 0.390, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.515. Electronics declined from the previously reported 0.400; unchanged macro performance does not establish a benefit from endpoint weighting. The isolated change applied an eight-transition half-life relative to each supplied training window’s final target, with weights normalized within each history. This result does not support that weighting hypothesis under the current configuration; it does not establish why performance failed to improve. Allocated GPU time was 433.89 seconds.
code_summary: One independently trained SASRec per category: 96-dimensional embeddings, two causal Transformer blocks, two attention heads, dropout 0.2, and maximum sequence length 64. Predictions use normalized sequence/item embeddings, a jointly learned bounded scale, and jointly learned item biases. Training retains sampled-softmax cross-entropy with 256 sampled negatives, training-history exclusion masks, prefix augmentation, and at most 24 sampled transitions per history. Transition losses receive weights 2^(-d/8), normalized per history before equal averaging across valid histories. AdamW, learning-rate decay, validation checks, early stopping, and single-best-checkpoint selection remain unchanged. Dataset routing loads exactly one checkpoint per category; no ensembles or separately fitted scorers are used.
